title: Math professor automates Canvas upkeep with Codex, saving 4-5 hours a week
summary: Cal State math professor Taiyo Inoue had Codex write scripts against Canvas's API to keep his courses updated, then used the freed time to flip his classes toward in-class group problem-solving.
agent_role: Codex generated and ran Python scripts against the Canvas API; Inoue described what he needed and checked the course updates.
outcome: Inoue estimates Codex saves him roughly four to five hours a week
what_they_did: Cal State math professor Taiyo Inoue used Codex to generate Python scripts that talk to Canvas's API, the interface other programs use to update Canvas. He is not a programmer but knows enough Python to describe what he wants. The scripts update course shells, shift materials to a new academic calendar, adapt to different meeting patterns and create timely announcements.
how_it_went: Inoue estimates Codex saves him roughly four to five hours a week. In demos he can start from a blank Canvas shell and fill in a full semester of materials. He used the time to flip his classes so students solve problems together at whiteboards.
worth_knowing: The source is OpenAI's own blog. Inoue also uses this low-stakes admin workflow to show AI-skeptical faculty where AI can help without raising cheating concerns.
prompt: Help me automate upkeep of my Canvas course [course name] using the Canvas API. I need Python scripts that: shift all assignment due dates and materials from [old term dates] to [new term dates], adapt the schedule to a [meeting pattern, e.g. Tuesday/Thursday] pattern, upload files from [folder], and draft announcements for [events]. Explain how to create and safely store an API token for [your institution's Canvas URL]. Start with read-only scripts that list what would change. Show me the planned changes and wait for my approval before writing anything to the live course. If possible, test on a sandbox course first.
